articles.title_en: Review of MXene-Based Polymer–Metal Oxide Hybrids for Energy Storage
articles.summary_en: This comprehensive review examines multifunctional MXene–polymer–metal oxide hybrids for next-generation energy-storage devices. It synthesizes material designs and performance considerations, highlighting MXene-based hybrid architectures as a research pathway for improved storage technologies.

articles.title_original: Research Progress of Hexagonal Boron Nitride in Lubrication
articles.title_en: Review Highlights h-BN Advances for Lubrication Applications
articles.excerpt_original: Hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) is a lubricant additive with considerable application potential. Its layered structure provides low interlayer shear strength, while its favorable thermal stability, chemical inertness, and electrical insulation make it attractive for demanding lubrication environments. However, the tribological performance of h-BN depends not only on interlayer sliding but also on the combined effects of material structure, lubricant medium, and operating conditions. Its practical application is further constrained by insufficient compatibility with certain media, inefficient delivery into the contact zone, and limited retention at the sliding interface, thereby compromising sustained friction reduction and wear protection. This review focuses on the structure-interface-performance relationships of h-BN-based lubricant additives and summarizes advances in size and morphology control, surface functionalization, and composite design, with particular emphasis on how these strategies affect the dispersion of h-BN in lubricant media, its delivery to the contact zone, and its participation in interfacial protective layers. The tribological behavior of h-BN-based additives under different lubricant media and service conditions is further compared to clarify their effective performance windows and practical application boundaries. Finally, the key challenges that remain in controlled synthesis and structural regulation, dynamic interfacial evolution, and service-oriented performance validation are summarized, providing a framework for material structural design, mechanistic analysis, and application-specific assessment.
articles.summary_en: This review examines hexagonal boron nitride as a lubricant additive, focusing on its low interlayer shear strength, thermal stability, chemical inertness, and electrical insulation. It assesses how particle size, morphology, surface functionalization, and composite design influence dispersion, delivery, friction reduction, and wear protection, while identifying remaining application challenges.

articles.title_original: Taming Gas-Phase Radical Contributions to the Oxidative Dehydrogenation of Propane by Tailoring Defect Structures in Boron Nitride
articles.title_en: Defect-engineered boron nitride improves propane oxidative dehydrogenation
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) is a promising catalyst for highly selective oxidative dehydrogenation of propane (ODHP). Defect engineering exposes unsaturated boron (B) sites, which form oxy/hydroxylated B-based active ensembles (i.e., B(OH)xO3–x) that are crucial for ODHP. The reaction proceeds via both surface and gas-phase radical pathways, making it critical to clarify the gas-phase contribution over N-defective h-BN. Here, we synthesized a series of N-defective BN (BN-x) samples via an N-repair strategy. Catalytic evaluation and in situ diffuse reflectance Fourier transform infrared spectra (DRIFTS) reveal that BN-1, with the highest N defect density, achieves enhanced ODHP activity by exposing more B(OH)xO3–x active ensembles, as corroborated by X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES). Kinetic studies, void-space filling, and water co-feeding experiments collectively demonstrate that the number of defects in BN-1 helps tame the gas-phase pathway contribution in the ODHP. Density-functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that N-defect sites promote O2 dissociation, thereby inducing active >B–B–O• sites that increase the reactivity and stabilization of radicals (e.g., HOO•, C3H7•, and CH3•), leading to an increase in the contribution of the gas-phase pathway. Additionally, >B–B–O• facilitates i-C3H7 generation and initiates a gas phase reaction with a lower dehydrogenation barrier, and water-assisted active site regeneration is thermodynamically more favorable.
articles.summary_en: Researchers show that nitrogen-defective hexagonal boron nitride enhances oxidative dehydrogenation of propane by exposing active boron ensembles and influencing gas-phase radical pathways. Experiments and DFT calculations indicate that defect density promotes oxygen dissociation, radical stabilization, and water-assisted site regeneration.

articles.title_original: Mitigating Contact‐Constricted Thermal Bottlenecks by Magnetically Programmable hBN Bridge Fillers in Al 2 O 3 /Epoxy Composites
articles.title_en: Magnetically Aligned hBN Fillers Improve Thermal Conductivity in Insulating Epoxy Composites
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Thermally conductive polymer composites often suffer from limited heat transport due to contact constriction in spherical particulate networks. To address this challenge, we report a magnetically programmable bridge‐filler architecture that enhances thermal pathways in electrically insulating epoxy systems. In this design, spherical Al 2 O 3 serves as a process‐friendly primary filler framework, while Fe 3 O 4 ‐functionalized hexagonal boron nitride (hBN@Fe 3 O 4 ) flakes act as magnetically addressable bridge fillers that connect neighboring alumina particles and can be oriented along the through‐plane direction under an external magnetic field. At a fixed total filler loading of 40 vol%, the Al 2 O 3 :hBN@Fe 3 O 4 ratio of 8:2 provides the most effective balance between bridge‐network formation and rheological freedom for alignment, yielding a through‐plane thermal conductivity of 2.02 W m − 1 K − 1 , 72.8% higher than that of the corresponding Al 2 O 3 ‐only composite. Finite‐element modeling reveals that the hybrid aligned architecture alleviates point‐contact‐dominated thermal bottlenecks by redistributing heat flux through more continuous bridge‐mediated pathways. The optimized composite retains high volume resistivity (4.4 × 10 1 5 Ω cm) and lower dielectric constant and loss than the Al 2 O 3 composite, while package‐level thermal tests confirm faster heat transfer. These results establish a generalizable design principle for directionally efficient thermal management in electrically insulating composites with relevance to advanced electronic packaging.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used Fe₃O₄-functionalized hexagonal boron nitride flakes as magnetically aligned bridge fillers between alumina particles, increasing through-plane thermal conductivity by 72.8% to 2.02 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 40 vol% loading. The electrically insulating composite also retained high resistivity and demonstrated faster package-level heat transfer, supporting applications in electronic thermal management.

articles.title_original: Fabrication of Multilayer Alternating Polymer-based Dielectric Composites with Superior Energy Storage Performance via Layer-by-layer Spraying Assembly
articles.title_en: Multilayer polymer dielectric films deliver record energy-storage performance
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Polymer-based dielectric composites are pivotal for advanced pulsed power and power electronics, yet synergistically enhancing dielectric constant and breakdown strength remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a controllable layer-by-layer spray assembly strategy to fabricate ordered multilayer polyetherimide (PEI)-based composites with alternating high-dielectric and high-insulation layers. Homologous carboxylated PEI (CPEI) was designed and covalently grafted onto boron nitride nanosheets (BNNS) and barium strontium titanate (BST) fillers, ensuring exceptional interfacial compatibility. This enabled the precise deposition of CPEI@BNNS/PEI and CPEI@BST/PEI layers, yielding 3-, 5-, and 7-layer films. The 7-layer film achieved a high dielectric constant of 7.43 at 1 kHz, a remarkable breakdown strength of 731.2 kV·mm-1, and a record discharge energy density of 20.87 J·cm-3—4.91 times that of pure PEI—while maintaining >90% charge-discharge efficiency. Comprehensive characterization and simulations revealed that the alternating multilayer structure creates deep-level interface traps that effectively suppress space charge migration, homogenize the internal electric field, and block electrical tree propagation. This work provides a facile and scalable pathway for the design and fabrication of high-performance ultrathin dielectric films.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed layer-by-layer sprayed polyetherimide composites containing boron nitride nanosheets and barium strontium titanate. A seven-layer film achieved 20.87 J·cm⁻³ discharge energy density, 731.2 kV·mm⁻¹ breakdown strength, and over 90% efficiency, indicating potential for pulsed-power and power-electronics applications.

articles.title_original: Atomically thin amorphous carbon with an ultralow dielectric constant
articles.title_en: Atomically Thin Amorphous Carbon Demonstrates Ultralow-k Dielectric Performance
articles.excerpt_original: Two-dimensional (2D) materials could replace conventional electronic components. Key advances have already been made in applying 2D materials to integrated circuits, but a robust, atomically thin ultralow-k dielectric remains crucial for further circuit scaling. Minimizing parasitic capacitances, in particular, will be needed as conductor spacing shrinks below 10 nm. However, conventional amorphous or porous low-k dielectrics become unstable at nanometre thicknesses. Here we show that atomically thin amorphous carbon films can function as mechanically robust ultralow-k dielectrics with a dielectric constant of 1.35 and a dielectric strength of 28–31 MV cm−1. The films are also an effective barrier to metal-ion diffusion, with a time to failure of 1010 s at 0.8-nm thickness. Our approach relies on a low-temperature, direct and conformal growth process, which makes it promising for practical implementation in complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology. An amorphous carbon film with a dielectric constant of 1.35 can act as a robust ion-diffusion barrier, even at a thickness of 0.8 nm.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report mechanically robust amorphous carbon films with a dielectric constant of 1.35 and dielectric strength of 28–31 MV cm⁻¹. The 0.8-nm films also act as metal-ion diffusion barriers, indicating potential for advanced CMOS interconnect scaling.

articles.title_original: Photoconductive gain of extrinsic semiconductor detectors
articles.title_en: New model explains photoconductive gain in doped semiconductor detectors
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Photoconductive gain in extrinsic (doped) semiconductor devices has traditionally been described by the ratio of the constant carrier lifetime to the carrier transit time. In this work, the constant-lifetime approximation is replaced by an effective lifetime, obtained through spatial averaging of photocurrent density over device length, resulting in photocurrent saturation with applied voltage bias. The concept of effective mobility, which incorporates contributions from both majority and minority carriers, is introduced. Analytical expressions for effective carrier distributions based on effective mobility and for photoconductive gain governed by effective carrier distributions and majority-carrier photocurrent are derived. It is further shown that the maximum gain depends only on the ratio of majority to minority carrier mobilities, eliminating the unphysical prediction of unbounded gain at high bias voltages, extreme mobilities, or short device lengths. The analysis reconciles classical theory with simulation and experimental results, recovering correct gain behaviour across low- and high-drift regimes.
articles.summary_en: Researchers replace the conventional constant-lifetime approximation with an effective lifetime derived from spatial photocurrent averaging. The model predicts voltage-dependent photocurrent saturation and bounded gain governed by the mobility ratio of majority and minority carriers, aligning theory with simulations and experiments.

articles.title_original: Interfacial synergy-driven CM-MOF@2D hybrids: Graphene vs MXene for accelerated organic pollutant degradation under dark and solar irradiation
articles.title_en: Graphene–MOF Hybrids Enhance Dark and Solar Dye Degradation
articles.excerpt_original: Recently, for the removal of persistent organic dyes, it is important to design more efficient and sustainable catalysts for wastewater treatment. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising catalysts due to their tunable porosity and abundant active sites; however, poor charge transport and rapid recombination of charge carriers limit their catalytic activities. In this context, herein, bimetallic Cu/Mn-based MOFs (CM-MOF) were integrated with graphene and V2CTx MXene via a one-step hydrothermal route to investigate the role of these supports in catalytic dye removal. The direct growth of CM-MOF on 2D sheets ensured strong interfacial contact and uniform dispersion, as confirmed by structural and morphological analysis. The resulting composites were evaluated for the degradation of Congo red-CR and methyl orange-MO under both dark and natural sunlight. Compared to pristine CM-MOF, the CM-MOF@Graphene and CM-MOF@MXene exhibited significantly enhanced dye removal efficiency ((78% without sunlight under dark) and 99% under natural sunlight), which is attributed to improved adsorption characteristics, facilitated charge transport, and promoted surface redox activity. Hence, with a detailed comparison of MOF@2D materials for water purification, the study highlights their potential for both advanced wastewater treatment as well as other future scientific applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers integrated graphene with bimetallic copper–manganese metal-organic frameworks to improve charge transport, adsorption, and redox activity for wastewater treatment. The graphene hybrid achieved up to 99% dye removal under natural sunlight and 78% in dark conditions, outperforming pristine MOF catalysts.

articles.title_original: Substrate-induced charge transfer and optical quenching in monolayer semiconducting TMDCs
articles.title_en: Substrates Strongly Quench Optical Signals in Monolayer TMDCs
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The optical and electronic properties of a two-dimensional (2D) material are profoundly influenced by the nature of its underlying substrate, thereby making the substrate-material interactions a vital factor for both fundamental studies and technological applications. These interactions can significantly modify the electronic structure and optical response of the 2D system, providing a powerful means to tailor and optimize their properties. In this study, we employ optical spectroscopy, including Raman and photoluminescence (PL) measurements, to probe the effects of the substrate on monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs): tungsten disulfide (WS 2 ) and tungsten diselenide (WSe 2 ). The films were synthesized by the laser-assisted synthesis technique (LAST) on silicon/silicon dioxide (Si/SiO 2 ) substrates and subsequently transferred onto interdigitated Si–Si/SiO 2 platforms to study the effects of bare Si and Si/SiO 2 surfaces on these materials. The optical response of the 2D single crystals on bare Si and Si/SiO 2 substrates reveals pronounced substrate-induced modifications, underscoring the critical influence of the supporting surface. Portions of the monolayers of WS 2 and WSe 2 on the Si/SiO 2 areas of the interdigitated substrate showed strong Raman and PL signals, while on the bare Si regions, these signals were relatively weaker or strongly suppressed. Additionally, strong PL quenching, approximately 10-fold for WS 2 and 13-fold for WSe 2 , was evident. A slight shift in the PL peak was also observed, which was more pronounced in WSe 2 . We rationalize these observations via first-principles calculations identifying band alignments and surface interactions as the mechanisms producing the PL quenching in TMDCs on Si substrates. Our findings
articles.summary_en: Study finds that silicon substrates suppress photoluminescence in monolayer WS₂ and WSe₂ by approximately 10-fold and 13-fold, respectively, compared with Si/SiO₂ surfaces. First-principles calculations attribute the effect to substrate-induced band alignment and surface interactions, highlighting implications for 2D semiconductor device design.

articles.title_original: Optical Voltage Profiling of 2D Semiconductors via Proximal Exciton Sensing
articles.title_en: Optical technique maps voltage in 2D semiconductors
articles.excerpt_original: High contact resistances in atomically thin semiconductors often mask intrinsic electrical transport properties, particularly at low carrier densities where exotic correlated states emerge. We introduce optical voltage profiling, a noninvasive wide-field technique that replaces local voltage probes with a proximal monolayer MoSe$_2$ exciton sensor. Isolated by thin hexagonal boron nitride, this sensor converts the target's local electrostatic potential into spatially resolved modulations of exciton reflectance. Through pixel-wise in situ calibration, these signals yield quantitative two-dimensional voltage maps of an actively biased semiconductor device. Using this method, we demonstrate the carrier-density-driven metal-insulator transition in bilayer MoSe$_2$ and obtain channel resistances below 1 k$Ω$ despite M$Ω$-scale two-terminal resistances in the metallic region. The optically derived resistance exhibits a metal-insulator crossover near the resistance quantum $h/e^2$, and the voltage maps and reconstructed local conductivity reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity in both insulating and metallic regimes. Beyond resolving channel resistance under high contact-resistance conditions, the technique provides spatially resolved access to microscopic transport heterogeneity in functional van der Waals devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers introduce a noninvasive method using a monolayer MoSe₂ exciton sensor to produce spatially resolved voltage maps in actively biased 2D semiconductor devices. The technique reveals local conductivity and transport heterogeneity despite high contact resistance, including a metal–insulator transition in bilayer MoSe₂.

articles.title_original: Electronic Reconstruction at the Quasicrystal-Moiré Crossover in Twisted Bilayer Graphene
articles.title_en: Twisted Bilayer Graphene Shows Electronic Reconstruction Near 29° Twist
articles.excerpt_original: Large twist angles in twisted bilayer graphene are widely expected to be electronically trivial, with negligible interlayer coupling and no electronic reconstruction, in contrast to the rich moiré-driven band reconstruction and correlated physics that emerge at small twist angles. Here, we show that this paradigm breaks down near a twist angle of 29°, where the system crosses over between quasicrystalline and commensurate order. Atomic-resolution transmission electron microscopy directly reveals the coexistence of near-dodecagonal quasicrystalline symmetry and emerging moiré periodicity, indicating an intermediate, nonperiodic structural regime. Magnetotransport measurements uncover strong interlayer hybridization mediated by Umklapp scattering, manifested by magneto-intersubband oscillations and a highly unconventional Landau-level spectrum. Remarkably, the Landau-level degeneracy evolves from 4- to 12-fold with increasing temperature, a behavior incompatible with two decoupled graphene monolayers. These findings establish large-angle twisted bilayer graphene as a platform where quasiperiodic symmetry fundamentally reshapes low-energy electronic states beyond the conventional moiré framework.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report strong interlayer hybridization and unconventional Landau-level behavior in twisted bilayer graphene near the quasicrystal–moiré crossover at a 29° twist angle. The findings identify large-angle twisted bilayer graphene as a platform for quasiperiodic control of low-energy electronic states.

articles.title_original: Valley-Polarized Transport in Graphene Induced by Asymmetric Strain and Ferromagnetic Modulation
articles.title_en: Strain and Ferromagnetic Modulation Enable Tunable Valley Transport in Graphene
articles.excerpt_original: In this work, we theoretically investigate the valley-dependent electron transport properties of graphene modulated by two strained regions and a single ferromagnetic stripe based on the Dirac equation and the transfer-matrix method. By constructing a multi-region model, the conductances of the K and K’ valleys as well as the corresponding valley polarization are systematically calculated. The effects of the magnetic vector-potential, the strain-induced gauge potentials, the widths of the strained regions, and the competition parameter λ on the valley-resolved transport behavior are analyzed in detail. The results show that both the conductance and the valley polarization are highly sensitive to the external modulation parameters and the geometric structural parameters. By properly tuning the relative strength and spatial distribution of the magnetic vector-potential and strain, an effective control of valley polarization can be achieved. This work deepens the understanding of valley-dependent transport mechanisms in graphene and provides theoretical guidance for tunable valley filtering in graphene-based systems.
articles.summary_en: Theoretical modeling shows that asymmetric strain and a ferromagnetic stripe can control valley-resolved conductance and polarization in graphene. The findings provide guidance for tunable valley filters and graphene-based valleytronic devices.

articles.title_original: Structured Evidence Dataset for Graphene-Enabled Hybrid Solar Systems Review
articles.title_en: Dataset Supports Evidence Review of Graphene-Enabled Hybrid Solar Systems
articles.excerpt_original: This dataset documents the structured evidence-control workflow underlying the critical review ‘From Graphene-Enabled Components to Integrated Hybrid Solar Systems: A Critical Review of Evidence, Integration Gaps, and Future Pathways.’ It contains (i) a claim-level article evidence matrix, (ii) a quantitative claim register identifying retained, qualified, and excluded numerical claims, and (iii) a citation crosswalk linking final manuscript reference numbers to permanent internal reference identifiers. The package is intended to improve transparency and traceability between scientific claims, evidence level, quantitative interpretation boundaries, and final citations. It contains derived review metadata only and does not redistribute copyrighted article full text or figures. Evidence levels are analytical boundaries used in the review and are not formal technology-readiness levels.
articles.summary_en: The dataset organizes claim-level evidence, quantitative claims, and citation links underpinning a critical review of graphene-enabled hybrid solar systems. It provides traceability and evidence boundaries but reports no new device performance or commercial deployment results.

articles.title_original: Development and characterisation of a novelaqueous graphene exfoliation method using triblock co-polymer, poloxamer 188
articles.title_en: Water-Based Graphene Exfoliation Using Poloxamer 188
articles.excerpt_original: Graphene is a two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterial that has garnered significant attention since its discovery in 2004 due to its unique physiochemical, electrical, mechanical, optical and thermal properties. Liquid phase exfoliation (LPE) is a versatile method of graphene production that is scalable and size-controllable, allowing for the exfoliation of graphene flakes tailored for specific applications. The use of water and biocompatible materials during exfoliation is particularly desirable as it bypasses the use of toxic organic exfoliants that restrict the application of the resultant graphene solutions. As such, there remains a need for the development of an efficient low-cost water-based graphite exfoliation method using environmentally favourable bio-surfactants for use in the biomedical sector. Therefore, the aim of this thesis was to develop a novel biologically relevant method of exfoliating hydrophobic graphite in water using a medically approved non-ionic triblock co-polymer and test its utility for different biological applications.Chapter 2 aimed to establish a method to produce high-quality graphene through surfactant-assisted LPE in water using the medically approved poloxamer 188 (P188) as a bio-surfactant. The successful exfoliation and stabilisation of graphene in water was achieved through the screening of several conditions such as, sonication time, concentration and temperature to produce aqueous soluble, few-layer P188 coated graphene sheets (P188-graphene), which were fully validated using electron microscopy. The exfoliated P188-graphene exhibited excellent long-term (6-week) stability in water. In addition, live cell imaging of the interaction of the exfoliated graphene with human cells showed that the material did not induce adverse morphologica
articles.summary_en: A thesis developed a water-based liquid-phase exfoliation method using medically approved poloxamer 188, producing stable, few-layer graphene dispersions. Initial cell imaging indicated no adverse morphological effects, supporting potential biomedical applications, though further evidence is needed.

articles.title_original: Synergistic graphene–ZnO composite electrode for Cartap sensing: Electrochemical behavior with DFT-based adsorption
articles.title_en: Graphene–ZnO Electrode Enables Electrochemical Cartap Detection
articles.excerpt_original: The detection of pesticide residues, including cartap, is crucial because of their environmental persistence and possible effects on ecosystems and human health, hence requiring the establishment of straightforward and dependable analytical techniques. This study presents the development of a graphene–ZnO (Gr/ZnO) nanocomposite-modified electrode for the electrochemical detection of cartap using cyclic voltammetry (CV). The electrochemical response of cartap was assessed at bare, graphene, ZnO, and Gr/ZnO-modified electrodes. The bare electrode displayed an oxidation peak between 0.1 and 0.2 V, whereas graphene exhibited a peak at approximately 0.1 V. ZnO exhibited an oxidation peak at approximately 0.7 V, while the Gr/ZnO composite demonstrated a displaced peak at around 0.6 V, signifying the synergistic effect of graphene conductivity and ZnO surface activity. The sensor exhibited a limit of detection (LOD) of 187.56 μmol L −1 with excellent linearity (R 2 = 0.99). Scan rate investigations indicated a surface-controlled mechanism, whereas Tafel analysis revealed unique charge transfer characteristics for the composite system. The electrode demonstrated satisfactory reproducibility, stability, and selectivity in the presence of interfering substances. Moreover, density functional theory (DFT) and adsorption analyses indicated a favorable interaction between cartap and the Gr/ZnO surface, elucidating the sensing mechanism. The investigation revealed that the Gr/ZnO composite provided an efficient and straightforward substrate for the electrochemical detection of cartap.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a graphene–ZnO nanocomposite electrode for detecting the pesticide cartap, combining graphene conductivity with ZnO surface activity. The sensor showed strong linearity, reproducibility, stability, and selectivity, although its reported detection limit indicates further sensitivity improvements may be needed.

articles.title_original: Evaluation of the Electrochemical Performance of MXene-Based Nanocomposites for Supercapacitor Applications
articles.title_en: Review evaluates MXene nanocomposites for high-performance supercapacitors
articles.excerpt_original: Supercapacitors offer high power density, fast charging/discharging capability, and long cycle life, yet their relatively low energy density limits broader deployment in electric vehicles, portable electronics, and grid storage systems. MXenes, a family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides, nitrides, and carbonitrides, have emerged as promising electrode materials due to their high electrical conductivity, tunable surface chemistry, hydrophilicity and intrinsic pseudocapacitive behavior. However, restacking of MXene layers reduces accessible surface area and ion transport efficiency, constraining electrochemical performance. To address this limitation, MXene-based nanocomposites incorporating carbon nanomaterials, conducting polymers, and metal oxides have been extensively developed. This review systematically evaluates recent advances in MXene-based nanocomposites for high-energy-density supercapacitors, highlighting electrochemical performance. A quantitative benchmarking comparison with commonly used electrode materials, including graphene, carbon nanotubes, and activated carbon, is provided. Key challenges in synthesis, performance standardization, and stability are discussed, along with future prospects for developing safer and scalable production methods of MXene-based electrodes.
articles.summary_en: The review assesses MXene-based nanocomposites incorporating carbon nanomaterials, conducting polymers and metal oxides to mitigate layer restacking and improve ion transport. It benchmarks performance against graphene, carbon nanotubes and activated carbon while identifying synthesis, standardization and stability challenges.

articles.title_original: MXene-based electrocatalyst for the hydrogen evolution reaction: Innovations and advances – A review
articles.title_en: MXene Electrocatalysts for Hydrogen Evolution: Advances and Innovations
articles.summary_en: This review surveys MXene-based electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction, covering recent innovations, performance improvements, and underlying mechanisms. It highlights MXenes’ potential for advancing hydrogen-production technologies while outlining remaining research challenges.

articles.title_original: Thermo-hydraulic and second-law performance assessment of MXene ionanofluids in flat-plate solar collectors
articles.title_en: MXene ionanofluids improve solar-collector thermal performance
articles.excerpt_original: MXene-based ionanofluids are promising heat transfer fluids for solar thermal applications due to their superior thermophysical properties. This study evaluates their thermo-hydraulic and second-law performance in a flat-plate solar collector by integrating experimentally measured thermophysical properties with numerical simulations to identify the optimum operating conditions. To assess various parameters, including outlet temperature, surface temperature, heat transfer properties, pressure drop, pumping power, absorbed heat rate, energy efficiency, entropy generation, and performance index (PI), simulations were carried out over a practical inlet temperature range of 293.15–323.15 K and Reynolds numbers (Re) from 100 to 900. The numerical results demonstrate that MXene ionanofluids offer significant thermal enhancement with regulated hydraulic penalties. Thermal conductivity and specific heat capacity increase by roughly 53–54% and 16–17%, respectively, at 1 wt%, resulting in a heat transfer coefficient increase of up to 48–51% compared to the base fluid. When Re increases from 100 to 900, it can reduce the output temperature by up to 8.2% and enhance energy efficiency by roughly 111%. However, at higher nanoparticle concentrations, MXene incorporation reduced the pressure drop by up to 36%, thereby lowering the pumping power requirement. According to second-law analysis, system irreversibility is primarily due to thermal entropy generation, with frictional entropy accounting for less than 0.002% of the total. 0.2 wt% MXene ionanofluid is the ideal concentration, according to performance index analysis under equal pumping power settings, with PI values reaching 0.88 at 323.15 K. Overall, the study shows that MXene ionanofluids are attractive options for high-performan
articles.summary_en: A study finds that MXene-based ionanofluids can increase thermal conductivity by roughly 53–54% and heat-transfer coefficients by up to 48–51% in flat-plate solar collectors. Under equal pumping-power conditions, 0.2 wt% concentration produced the highest reported performance index, although higher flow rates improved efficiency while reducing outlet temperature.

articles.title_original: Thermal-electrical decoupling zone in graphene / hexagonal boron nitride polymer nanocomposites: dataset, effective-medium models and design maps
articles.title_en: Design maps for thermal–electrical decoupling in graphene/hBN polymer nanocomposites
articles.excerpt_original: Reproduction package for the manuscript Computational Mapping of the Thermal-Electrical Decoupling Zone in Graphene/Hexagonal Boron Nitride Polymer Nanocomposites (Advanced Theory and Simulations, manuscript ID 1005070). Contains the curated three-tier literature dataset of graphene and hexagonal boron nitride polymer composites, the record-level screening log documenting every inclusion and exclusion decision, the calibrated Lewis-Nielsen and McLachlan generalized-effective-medium implementations, the Latin-hypercube design set with its fixed seed, and the scripts that regenerate every figure, table and design rule reported in the article. Code is released under the MIT Licence; data under CC BY 4.0.
articles.summary_en: An open reproduction package provides a curated literature dataset, screening records, effective-medium models, design sets, and scripts for mapping thermal–electrical decoupling in graphene and hexagonal boron nitride polymer composites. The release supports reproducible analysis and design-rule generation, but does not report a commercial product or industrial deployment.

articles.title_original: Hydrophilicity-reduced hexagonal-BN supported Cu/ZnO-based catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol
articles.title_en: Exfoliated h-BN Support Improves Cu/ZnO Catalyst for Methanol Production
articles.excerpt_original: Cu/ZnO/Al 2 O 3 has been a common catalyst for CO 2 hydrogenation to methanol. However, this catalyst suffered from water deactivation by the reaction product water, leading to reduced catalyst activity. In this research, hexagonal boron nitride (hexagonal-BN) was used as a hydrophilicity-reduced support for Cu/ZnO-based catalyst, with pretreatment of modified Hummers’ method to perform exfoliation and OH-group functionalization on hexagonal-BN to form H-hBN. Cu/ZnO-based catalyst with Al, La, or Ga as promoter metal and a trace amount of Mg was synthesized by the co-precipitation method. The results showed that CuZnAlMg/H-hBN catalyst exhibited the utmost methanol space-time yield among others at 230 °C and 5 MPa, and could achieve an even higher methanol space-time yield value at 270 °C and 5 MPa, reaching 201.1 mg CH3OH /g cat -h. Catalyst characterization indicated that catalysts with H-hBN as a support could exhibit reduced hydrophilicity and increased water-removal ability. Moreover, using H-hBN could increase the catalyst's Cu dispersion, thereby improving catalyst activity. Therefore, CuZnAlMg/H-hBN showed a high percentage of active Cu sites, resulting in its high methanol space-time yield. In summary, hexagonal BN is an innovative catalyst support that reduces catalyst hydrophilicity and increases water-removal capacity, leading to enhanced CO 2 hydrogenation for methanol production.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a hydrophilicity-reduced hexagonal boron nitride-supported Cu/ZnO catalyst for CO₂ hydrogenation to methanol. The modified support improved water removal and copper dispersion, with the CuZnAlMg/H-hBN formulation achieving a reported methanol space-time yield of 201.1 mg/g catalyst-hour at 270 °C and 5 MPa.

articles.title_original: Carrier-controlled reconfigurable mid-IR hyperbolicity in ZnO via phonon-plasmon coupling
articles.title_en: Doped ZnO Enables Reconfigurable Mid-IR Hyperbolic Dispersion
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Natural hyperbolic materials (NHMs) are attractive materials for mid-infrared nanophotonics but typically offer fixed and narrow hyperbolic bands set by optical phonons. Here, we demonstrate that free-carrier control in ZnO enables phonon–plasmon hybridization that reconfigures the mid-IR permittivity and allows the emergence of both Type I and Type II hyperbolic dispersions with substantially expanded bandwidths. Using infrared spectroscopic ellipsometry and uniaxial Kukharskii‑model fits, we reveal the characteristic anti‑crossing and Rabi‑type splitting of the hybrid longitudinal phonon–plasmon branches as the plasma energy approaches the longitudinal optical phonon energy, inducing an optical topological transition between hyperbolic types. Full‑vector Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) simulations confirm the emergence and evolution of hyperbolic modes across phonon‑like, strong‑coupling, and plasmon‑like regimes and quantify the associated field-intensity enhancements. Our results establish doped ZnO as a tunable, naturally hyperbolic platform in the mid-IR and outline a practical route to engineer negative real permittivity bands, switch hyperbolic topology, and design reconfigurable polaritonic functionalities by adjusting the carrier density and losses through various growth and post-processing techniques.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrate carrier-controlled phonon–plasmon coupling in ZnO that switches between Type I and Type II hyperbolic dispersion while expanding the usable mid-infrared bandwidth. The work positions doped ZnO as a tunable platform for reconfigurable polaritonic and nanophotonic devices.

articles.title_original: Efficient graphene electro-optic modulation via maximized optical mode overlap
articles.title_en: Embedded graphene design boosts silicon photonic modulator efficiency
articles.excerpt_original: Integrating more components in one silicon photonic chip is critical for processing exponentially growing data in optical communications and photonic computing. One of the key components in the chip, the electro-optic modulator, suffers from an oversized footprint (in millimeters). Graphene modulators are more compact, with device sizes at hundreds of micrometers. However, conventional graphene-on-top configurations, where graphene only couples to the weak evanescent field of the waveguide, have limited modulation efficiency and hinder the continuing efforts of reducing device footprint. Here, we present a design where graphene layers are positioned inside the optical mode to maximize light-graphene interaction. This architecture enhances the effective refractive index modulation and shows 30% increased efficiency compared to the conventional design, which facilitates a 3 dB bandwidth exceeding 30 GHz. Wafer-scale manufacturing with graphene integrated at the Back End of Line (BEOL) is achieved. As an additional proof-of-concept demonstration, a silicon-platform embedded graphene modulator achieves a modulation efficiency of 0.096 V·cm. We believe this work provides a pathway for graphene integrating to high-density, foundry-level silicon photonic circuits.
articles.summary_en: Researchers embedded graphene layers within the optical mode of silicon waveguides, increasing modulation efficiency by 30% versus conventional graphene-on-top designs. The architecture achieved bandwidth above 30 GHz and wafer-scale BEOL integration, supporting denser silicon photonic circuits.

articles.title_original: Probing the potential profile of twisted bilayer graphene via Fabry-Pérot interference
articles.title_en: Fabry–Pérot interference maps potential barriers in twisted bilayer graphene
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract We use Fabry-Pérot interference to probe the internal potential profile of large-angle twisted bilayer graphene. We trace anomalous resistance oscillations in the nominally unipolar regime to a hidden cavity formed by unintentional local doping in our device. By analyzing zero-field interference patterns, we determine the location and size of this inhomogeneity. Magnetotransport measurements support the model, distinguishing local cavity modes from global resonances through their different magnetic dependence. Simulations using our extracted profile reproduce the experimental features. Our results highlight interference spectroscopy as a simple, non-invasive probe for identifying local defects and internal potential barriers in ballistic devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used Fabry–Pérot interference and magnetotransport to identify hidden cavities caused by local doping in large-angle twisted bilayer graphene. The method provides a non-invasive way to locate internal defects and potential barriers in ballistic graphene devices.

articles.source: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
articles.title_original: An Acid-Activated Graphene Oxide Ferroptosis Rheostat for Plaque-Targeted Atherosclerosis Therapy
articles.title_en: Acid-Activated Graphene Oxide Platform Targets Atherosclerotic Plaques
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Background Atherosclerotic plaques contain acidic, iron-rich niches in which lipid peroxidation and inflammation reinforce one another. Single-pathway interventions are therefore unlikely to restore local redox balance. We developed GO@Drug, a graphene oxide (GO) nanoplatform that co-delivers quercetin and β-sitosterol to modulate ferroptosis and inflammation within plaques. Results Under acidic conditions, GO catalysed Fe 3+ reduction to Fe 2+ , creating a localized redox input. Quercetin engaged the AKT1-GPX4 antioxidant pathway, whereas β-sitosterol suppressed IL-1β-driven inflammatory signaling, together restoring redox homeostasis in macrophage foam cells. Catalytic attenuation of GO, AKT1 knockout, or IL-1β reconstitution weakened the therapeutic response, confirming contributions from both the material and the loaded drugs. In ApoE-/- mice, GO@Drug accumulated in plaques, reduced lesion burden, increased fibrous cap thickness, and restored ferroptosis-associated redox balance without detectable systemic toxicity. Plaque-specific Fe 2+ imaging and radiolabel tracking further showed local activation and gradual clearance. Conclusions These findings identify GO as an active redox modulator and support a microenvironment-responsive strategy for controlling ferroptosis-inflammation coupling in atherosclerosis.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed GO@Drug, a graphene oxide platform that co-delivers quercetin and β-sitosterol to regulate ferroptosis and inflammation in acidic, iron-rich plaques. In ApoE−/− mice, the platform reduced lesion burden and increased fibrous cap thickness without detectable systemic toxicity, but the findings remain preclinical.

articles.title_original: Effect of Ammonium Chloride Electrolyte on the Performance of Graphene Nano Sheets Electrode
articles.title_en: Ammonium Chloride Modification Improves Graphene Nanosheet Battery Electrodes
articles.excerpt_original: Research on the effect of ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl) electrolyte on graphene nanosheet (GNS) electrodes derived from candlenut shells (Aleurites moluccana (L.) Willd.) as primary battery cathodes has been conducted. GNS was synthesized via pyrolysis and modified with NH₄Cl to produce G–N 0.5 M, G–N 1.0 M, G–N 2.0 M, and G–N 3.0 M samples. The materials were characterized using XRD, SEM-EDX, BET, electrical measurements at 0.5–1.5 V, CV, and GCD. XRD results show peaks at 2θ ≈ 25° and 44.27° corresponding to C(002) and C(100) planes, while G–N samples exhibit new diffraction peaks at (111), (200), (220), (311), (222), and (400), indicating NH₄Cl incorporation. SEM analysis reveals a transition from layered GNS morphology to more wrinkled and agglomerated structures with increasing NH₄Cl concentration, supported by EDX showing decreasing carbon content and the presence of chlorine (up to ~5.9%). articles.title_original: Photo-induced interfacial charge transfer in solar-responsive PVDF composite membranes

articles.excerpt_original: Solar-driven membrane distillation (SDMD) using advanced composite membranes offers promise for sustainable water purification. Here, we present an atomistic computational study of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membranes incorporating hexagonal boron nitride (BN) and tungsten nitride (WN) nanofillers to elucidate the mechanisms underlying photoinduced charge transfer and photothermal excitation. We use a hierarchical multiscale framework integrating density functional theory (DFT), time-dependent DFT perturbation theory, and classical molecular dynamics to assess the electronic, optical, and structural properties of PVDF/BN/WN composites. Our calculations reveal a dramatic narrowing of the band gap from pristine PVDF (5.41 eV) to 0.57 eV in the composite, driven by orbital hybridization and enhanced interfacial charge transfer. Low-energy optical absorption (~ 0.85 eV) associated with charge-transfer transitions and collective excitations in WN clusters, alongside broadband activity from the near-infrared to the ultraviolet, is predicted. Molecular dynamics simulations confirm structural stability and strong interfacial ordering, with realistic atomic densities and constrained polymer mobility. These findings provide quantitative insight into the interplay between nanofiller-induced electronic structure modulation and membrane stability, establishing a theoretical foundation for designing PVDF-based composite membranes for efficient solar-driven water purification and related energy applications.
articles.summary_en: Computational modeling indicates that adding boron nitride and tungsten nitride nanofillers to PVDF membranes can substantially narrow the band gap and enable broadband photoabsorption. This strictly two-dimensional, atomically thin material exhibits outstanding crystalline quality and exceptional electronic properties. Despite its relatively short history in scientific investigation, graphene has already demonstrated a wide range of emerging physical phenomena and significant application potential. In this study, the electronic structure of AAA-stacked the trilayer graphene is comprehensively examined. In this configuration, the first and third layers are kept fixed, while the middle layer is rotated by 0°, 21.79°, 38.21°, and 60°, respectively. The calculations are performed within the framework of Density Functional Theory (DFT) using the Quantum ESPRESSO computational package. The results indicate that the electronic characteristics of the trilayer graphene are strongly influenced by the stacking arrangement of the layers. Specifically, in the AAA configuration, rotation of the middle layer at the specified angles leads to the formation of a zero-energy semi-metallic gap, highlighting the fundamental role of interlayer interactions and orientation in governing the electronic behavior of this system.

articles.title_original: Engineering kekule superconductivity from layer-selective interactions in rhombohedral graphene
articles.title_en: Study predicts Kekulé superconductivity in multilayer graphene
articles.excerpt_original: At weak coupling, finite-momentum superconductivity is typically associated with broken time-reversal or inversion symmetry of the Fermi surface. Here, we show that lattice-scale pair-density-wave order in rhombohedral multilayer graphene can arise from layer/orbital-dependent pairing interactions, band chirality, and Dirac-point-centered Fermi surface topology while preserving both symmetries. Using mean-field theory and comparing finite momentum sectors $Q = \pm 2 K_{D}$ with the $ Q = 0$ superconducting state, we find that layer-dependent interactions of opposite signs ($V_{1A}=-V_{JB}=-|V|$) favor an intra-valley Kekulè state with center-of-mass momentum ($ Q=\pm 2 K_D$). In the presence of a time-reversal and inversion symmetry-preserving Kane-Mele mass ($λ$), this state appears only above a critical carrier density ($n^{crit}_{K}(λ,J)$). The two superconducting condensates exhibit opposite chirality, $J(-J)$ for $K_D(-K_D) $ valleys, thereby preserving time-reversal and inversion symmetry. We map the phase diagram and analyze the dependence of $T_c$ on the chirality index $J$ and $λ$. We also evaluate the superfluid stiffness in the Kekulè superconducting state, thereby determining the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition temperature. Our results show that orbital-dependent interactions in the presence of band chirality favor finite-momentum pairing in time-reversal and inversion symmetric Dirac materials.
articles.summary_en: Theoretical work shows that layer- and orbital-dependent interactions can produce finite-momentum Kekulé superconductivity in rhombohedral multilayer graphene while preserving time-reversal and inversion symmetry. It maps the required carrier density, chirality, mass, and BKT-transition conditions, offering design guidance for superconducting Dirac materials.

articles.title_original: Ferroelectric-assisted charge-transfer plasmons in graphene/CuInP2S6
articles.title_en: Graphene/CuInP2S6 heterostructures enable switchable charge-transfer plasmons
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Two-dimensional materials and their van der Waals heterostructures provide a versatile platform for novel optoelectronic functionalities. Interfacial charge transfer in such stacks enables high-quality graphene plasmons, but the charge-doping is fixed by work-function differences between constituent layers. Ferroelectric substrates have been explored for non-volatile, switchable doping, yet oxide ferroelectrics yield only modest doping due to imperfect interfaces. Here, we report efficient charge transfer between graphene and the van der Waals ferroelectric CuInP 2 S 6 , where the atomically-sharp interface yields unexpectedly large doping and high-quality plasmons, despite orders-of-magnitude smaller polarizations compared to oxide ferroelectrics. Infrared nano-imaging directly visualizes graphene plasmons whose doping depends on the adjacent ferroelectric layer. Combined nano-infrared and piezoresponse force microscopies reveal that graphene doping and CuInP 2 S 6 polarization increase with thickness and saturate in tandem, linking charge-transfer doping and out-of-plane ferroelectricity. Our results establish ferroelectric-assisted charge-transfer plasmons in graphene/CuInP 2 S 6 as a promising route to probe and control nanoscale ferroelectric textures.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report efficient charge transfer and high-quality graphene plasmons in heterostructures with the van der Waals ferroelectric CuInP2S6. Nano-imaging shows that graphene doping tracks ferroelectric polarization, suggesting a route for controlling nanoscale ferroelectric textures and optoelectronic functionality.

articles.title_original: A review of three-dimensional graphene photodetectors: advances in mechanisms, architectures, and applications
articles.title_en: Review Highlights 3D Graphene Photodetectors for Broadband Sensing
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract As a three-dimensional (3D) extension of two-dimensional (2D) graphene, it retains impressive properties such as high carrier mobility, electrical conductivity, and interfacial compatibility. Its unique porous network enhances optical field distribution and carrier dynamics, offering a higher specific surface area and greater active edge density than traditional semiconductor materials. This makes it an excellent candidate for advanced photodetection. Features such as nano-resonant cavities enhance light-absorption efficiency through photon confinement and scattering. Its zero-bandgap semimetallic nature enables devices to achieve a wide spectral response from the ultraviolet to the terahertz range. With a work function of 4.5 to 4.8 eV, 3D-graphene forms high-quality Schottky heterojunctions with semiconductors including silicon (Si), germanium (Ge), gallium arsenide (GaAs), and indium phosphide (InP), enhancing photogenerated charge carrier separation. Thus, 3D-graphene photodetectors show great potential for broadband response, high sensitivity, and compatibility with complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology. This review summarizes recent advances in 3D-graphene photodetectors, focusing on structural design and performance relationships while exploring applications in optoelectronic logic, polarization imaging, and information encryption.
articles.summary_en: A review examines how porous three-dimensional graphene architectures improve light absorption, carrier dynamics, and charge separation in photodetectors. The devices offer broadband ultraviolet-to-terahertz response and potential compatibility with CMOS, with applications including optoelectronic logic, polarization imaging, and information encryption.

articles.excerpt_original: We report the realization of a gate-defined quantum point contact (QPC) in bilayer graphene proximitized by a single aluminum superconducting electrode. Superconducting correlations induced in the ballistic channel enhance the conductance plateaus beyond their normal-state values. In addition, we observe a pronounced above-gap conductance anomaly which serves as a spectroscopic signature of the loss of superconductivity and the associated collapse of the Andreev excess current. By reconstructing the nonlinear current-voltage characteristics, we find that the magnitude of the excess current increases as successive QPC modes are populated. Additionally, we find that the switching current associated with the loss of superconductivity follows the underlying mode structure of the QPC, exhibiting discrete levels consistent with a heat dissipation-driven transition. These results demonstrate that the one-dimensional transport modes of the QPC govern both the equilibrium proximity effect and the non-equilibrium dynamics of the hybrid system.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated a gate-defined quantum point contact in bilayer graphene coupled to an aluminum superconducting electrode. The study shows that quantum point contact modes govern both superconducting transport and heat-dissipation-driven switching behavior, advancing understanding of graphene-based hybrid quantum devices.

articles.title_original: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes

articles.excerpt_original: MXenes, two-dimensional transition-metal carbides and nitrides, are typically obtained from MAX phases, yet historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. Here we combine machine-learning-assisted database mining with experiments to uncover overlooked multilayer (ml) MXenes. Screening of repositories reveals a "Treasure Chest" of 38 previously synthesized but unrecognized ml-MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we rediscover five MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature synthesis that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. Inspired by the identified chemistries, we further realize 11 previously unexplored rare-earth-based M2CT2 MXenes (M= Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd, Tb, Ho, and Tm). Experiments and theory reveal semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.
